Upper teal roof channels fork and merge into a narrow V/loop at the seam instead of a clean continuous cylindrical tile run.

Broad leaf silhouettes, vein scale and soft green illumination continue without an artificial horizontal band.

Gold roof ridge appears as a disconnected open bar beneath/offset from the finial base; teal roof covers the required joining location.

Gold rim and diagonal paving are locally joined, but dense fine repetitive stone texture persists.
Local gold rim and rounded teal tile lips maintain their direction and width through the horizontal seam.
Upper gold strip terminates in a sharp isolated tip with a visible gap before the new lower curl/ridge; original continuous roof-ridge identity is broken.
Central gold curve is continuous, but the far-right teal tile lips change phase/fork near the adjoining cross point.
Local teal/gold edge is continuous; quiet grey ground requirement still fails due repetitive fine hatch.
Four-way local foliage field stays coherent with rounded overlapping leaves and no visible cross-shaped strip boundary.
A small detached green leaf sprig floats in the paving away from the canopy; dense fine grey pattern remains.
Local ground plane has no obvious hard cross seam, but broad faces are filled with repetitive diamond/cellular strokes.

Teal channels widen/narrow into multiple doubled caps and irregular forked tile lips at the cross point.
Gold curl is closed, but lower/central neighboring tile channels form a fork/doubled cap without the needed ridge separation; right stone retains fine repetitive hatch.
Gold ridge has a sharp cut point and a visible gap to the lower gold curl; no continuous structural connection.
Roof channels form pinched V-shaped forks and a long flat tile fragment instead of a continuous same-width cylindrical tile run.
Roof channels merge into a large irregular Y/V crease, with crossing tile lips and abrupt lane scale changes.
